messages:
maria: quick ask — can someone run a short egress throughput + p99 latency smoke on dc2 on-prem? dashboard shows ~30% higher tails vs hosted for the same model and seq len. not sure if it's network or socket slowpath.

aj: I can take this in a few. can you paste the exact model/seq and the pod/node?

maria: model: redwood/turbo-3b-v1, seq=1024, batch=1. repro on node gpudc2-05 and gpudc2-07. started after the kernel bump last week.

bench-bot: scheduled benchmark run 1912345689 by aj — iperf3/kv-cache/throughput profile. results will land in #perf-artifacts.

kyle: before we run, quick checklist: MTU, GRO/TSO, rps/xps, irq affinity. last time MTU was 1500 on on-prem vs 9000 in hosted which bit us on small RPCs.

sam: agree. also check socket buffers and net.core.rmem_default/rmem_max. here's the exact iperf command I use for tokenized-ish loads:

```
# run on target node (server)
iperf3 -s -p 5201
# run from loadgen
iperf3 -c gpudc2-05 -p 5201 -t 30 -P 8 -w 512K --single_udp
```

sam: for tcp small RPCs use -P 16 -w 256K and measure retransmits.

devon: are we sure it's not the kube CNI? which CNI are we on for dc2 (calico/hostrouting vs flannel)?

maria: dc2 uses calico + eBPF host-routing. I validated policy no-nat for our subnets.

aj: running iperf now on gpudc2-05 -> gpudc2-01 to collect baseline. will also pull /proc/interrupts and ethtool stats.

kyle: if it's on the slowpath from user->kernel, we might see high syscall counts on sendmsg. can you run perf top on the runtime process during a short workload? pipeline:

```
sudo perf record -F 99 -g -p <pid> -o /tmp/perf.data -- sleep 20
sudo perf report -i /tmp/perf.data --stdio | head -n 40
```

kyle: look for sendto/sendmsg/epoll_wait hotspots.

aj: iperf3 tcp 30s run: throughput avg 2.1Gbits/s, retransmits 0. but p99 lat in runtime still high (~220ms) during generation. attaching quick kernel stats:

```
# /proc/interrupts (snippet)
16:  120000      0   PCI-MSI-edge  eth0
17:   90000      0   PCI-MSI-edge  eth1
# ethtool -S eth0 shows rx_packets high, rx	error 0
```

aj: also saw softirq steal around the p99 spikes.

devon: can you check XPS/RPS settings? sometimes defaulting to single queue kills p99 when CPU affinity not set.

maria: quick dump of runtime obs (truncated):

```
[2026-03-15T10:12:34Z] request id=rc_239 latency=220ms model=redwood/turbo-3b-v1 seq=1024 stage=kv-cache-lookup
[2026-03-15T10:12:34Z] cpu=3 pid=24567 syscall=sendmsg time_wait=12ms
[2026-03-15T10:12:34Z] request id=rc_240 latency=18ms model=redwood/turbo-3b-v1 seq=1024 stage=compute
```

maria: seems like some requests stall on kv-cache-lookup/sendmsg path.

sam: curious if the kernel bump changed GRO/TX offload behavior. can you check `ethtool -k eth0` and grep for tso/gro/gso?

aj: ethtool -k eth0 shows tso: on gso: on gro: on. no obvious toggles.

kyle: if offloads are on but we see syscall stalls, try toggling GRO off to see if it improves p99 (sometimes reduces batching delay for small requests).

devon: also try `echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/core/softirq_affinity` or adjust rps_cpus for rx queue CPU steering.

maria: plan: aj will run perf+iperf and flip GRO off for one node (gpudc2-05) for a quick 30m window and report results. kyle will prepare perf script to collect top stacks for sendmsg path. sam will run an isolated microbenchmark that reproduces rpc pattern. devon will validate CNI queues and XPS/RPS settings.

aj: starting GRO toggle now on gpudc2-05, running iperf/bench and the runtime smoke. will post results in ~20m.

bench-bot: perf artifact uploaded: https://perf.internal/reports/1912345689 (contains iperf logs + perf.data)

aj: quick summary after toggling GRO off: p99 dropped from ~220ms -> ~70ms on gpudc2-05 under same load. throughput unchanged.

maria: huge — that points to batching delays in kernel network stack. can we make this change cluster-wide or at least for the runtime nodes? need ops approval for kernel param changes.

devon: will open infra ticket with the change + rollback plan. include canary plan: roll to 10% of nodes, monitor p99 and CPU.

kyle: also schedule a kernel-bisect to see which commit altered behavior. leave GRO toggle in our playbook for now.

maria: thanks everyone. follow-ups: infra ticket + perf artifacts linked. I'll update the private dashboard with canary wheels when ticket is ready. :thumbsup:

aj: thanks — will keep the artifacts and perf flamegraphs in the ticket.

sam: nice catch.

maria: closing loop — if anyone wants to see the perf report ping me and I'll drop the raw perf.data.
